raw_chat.content: You have reached the step limit. Do not call any more tools. Reply now with your final answer: a short summary of what you found and what you changed.

The issue was caused by `TimestampCallback` failing to handle time units when the dataset uses a "code" unit system. When `self.time_unit` is a `Symbol` (which happens in code unit systems), it does not have a `latex_representation()` method. The code was catching this `AttributeError` but then explicitly raising a `RuntimeError` if `plot.ds._uses_code_time_unit` was true, which is exactly the condition that triggered the bug.

I modified `yt/visualization/plot_modifications.py` to handle this gracefully. Instead of raising a `RuntimeError`, the `except AttributeError` block now uses the string representation of the unit if `latex_representation()` fails, ensuring that `annotate_timestamp()` works correctly with code units.

Summary of changes:
- `yt/visualization/plot_modifications.py`: Modified `TimestampCallback.__call__` to avoid raising `RuntimeError` when `time_unit.latex_representation()` fails in code unit systems. It now falls back to the string representation of the unit.
